purpose: Reuse the existing persistent box write-and-restart path for exact private provider identifiers without adding a route, shell, SSH path, settings service, or model capability.
required_checks: B1_TEST_PYTHON=<existing-project-python> live/tools/b1_verify.sh
selected Python imports flask, flask_socketio, and requests before any suite starts
all bounded tests pass with every provider transition mocked
syntax compilation is in-memory and a read-only verifier run creates no repository bytecode or other candidate artifact

model-seat transport is the exact top-level curl --disable --config - command, --disable is first, a hostile user curl default is ignored, and the inherited host proxy, DNS, and TLS trust environment remains the admitted platform boundary
caller deploy JSON contains exactly action, target, signoff_block_id, and commit_sha

initial model grants remain unchanged; deploy-only admission derives elevation at the authority boundary, is pending, HIGH-IMPACT, uses an exact JSON-integer TTL of at most 300 seconds, carries one exact block-commit-target scope, and requires explicit operator confirmation of that displayed scope

the signed capability and private issued registry row carry the identical deploy scope, MAIN rejects a different block, commit, or target before relay, and ordinary capabilities cannot carry deploy scope

persisted request creation times, issued expiries, revocation times, transition creation times, and trusted deployment state timestamps are exact nonnegative JSON integers; strings, floats, and booleans fail closed before authorization or state reuse

proposal and latest signoff carry the identical canonical deploy ref for the requested commit and main, farm, or both scope; capability-authenticated deploy caller equals the mailbox signer and the two-party author/signer distinction remains enforced
ledger begin failure prevents mutation and every post-begin path attempts ledger finish
pre-mutation state is mode 600, atomic, directory-fsynced, globally locked, strictly bounded, and UNKNOWN never retries automatically
provider URL, authentication header, token, project, environment, services, queries, deployment ID, log options, timeout, redirect policy, and bounds are server-owned

trusted provider execution is exact argv curl --config - with shell disabled, private config only on stdin, a fresh minimal child environment with curl-specific default-config isolation and no general HOME/XDG overrides, HTTPS-only protocol, redirects disabled, fixed connect timeout and max-time 8, a fixed process deadline, body bound plus exact three-digit HTTP status capture, explicit 2xx enforcement, and no alternate Python HTTP path

MAIN and box reject deploy query parameters, wrong content types, oversized or invalid JSON, duplicate keys at every nesting level, nonobjects, missing or extra fields, and nonstring fields before dispatch
global state-lock acquisition is nonblocking and bounded to at most two seconds; state directories, files, and locks reject symlinks and nonregular objects

start and status validate stored provider, project, environment, and service identifiers against current trusted configuration before replay; status also binds the exact box-stored provider deployment ID and requested commit, and stale SUCCESS is rejected

terminal failure reads only a fixed bounded log query and returns no message text or message hash; severity output uses only a fixed vocabulary with unknown fallback, timestamps are strict timezone-bearing RFC3339 normalized to canonical UTC, and persisted summaries enforce availability, count, positive severity totals, and ordered timestamps
trusted_deploy.py installs beside box_ops.py and its adjacent-module fallback import is exercised
every manifest digest is exactly 64 lowercase hex, both manifests cover the exact overlay, and no rejected hosting-admin forward reference remains
git diff --check and high-confidence repository secret-pattern scan pass
review_questions: Can a caller provide or influence any provider fact, credential, identifier, request, log option, or transport choice?
Can a repeated start, response loss, concurrent process, or crash window cause a duplicate provider mutation?
Does an unknown mutation outcome require explicit operator reconciliation rather than an inferred absence or automatic retry?
Can status accept any deployment other than the exact stored ID with the fixed target service and requested commit?
Can any provider error body, token, build-log message, transformed message, or message hash reach the caller or either ledger?
Are initial capabilities unchanged, and is deploy elevation deploy-only, operator-confirmed, and cryptographically plus registry-bound to the exact reviewed block, commit, and target scope?
Can a capability holder reuse a signed block or capability for any different commit or target?
Do MAIN then burn-in then FARM preserve the rollback peer and fit existing transport timeouts?
Can another provider be added only by reviewed trusted server code without changing the caller contract?
live_resume_after_clean_review: require an independent ACCEPT of the exact manifest-frozen candidate bytes, then resolve the exact candidate HEAD mechanically
request operator authorization for that exact resolved HEAD before any push or live action; local commit state alone is never authority
install box_ops.py and trusted_deploy.py together with exact hash readback, then restart and verify under the rollback engine
deploy MAIN through operator recovery start/status, restart and prove burn-in, then deploy FARM through an elevated signer capability start/status
complete Control and Worker approval, denial, expiry, and revocation proofs
